name: Motorenwerk Saalach GmbH
summary: Motorenwerk Saalach is a 650-staff, group-owned motor maker (182 M EUR turnover) with sound finances, a stable credit index of 171 and an equity ratio of 30.2 %. It supplies 100 % of our IE4 30 kW motor (part:350013). It is refocusing on large key accounts, and its new sales director called our volume (0.6 % of its turnover) 'not strategic'. Replies have slowed, its latest quote is 'list conditions, supply from stock only', and it is annoyed that we pay late almost every time.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager up to 2 % price change; above 2 % the pricing committee (meets every two weeks); the new sales director sets account strategy

negotiation_pattern: At annual renewals it asks for moderate increases (2.4–3.9 %) and settles far lower: -1.5 %, then 0.0 %, then 1.7 %. The mean settlement is +0.07 % against a mean ask of 3.2 %. The price for part:350013 fell from the awarded 1671.86 (2024 quote) to 1608.32. It has given way on price within a fixed-per-year, list-based framework. It now protects list conditions and service level more actively and hints it will 'review conditions' if we keep paying late.
wants: on-time payment at the agreed 30 days net (its open grievance)
volume and key-account relevance (more spend per customer)
standard-range, stock-based business with low handling effort
price stability within list policy (no moves above 2 % that need committee approval)
protects: unit_price (list conditions; anything above 2 % needs the pricing committee)
payment_days (will not accept longer terms; already complaining about overdue invoices)
lead_time_days (42 days, now 'supply from stock only')

trades.give: payment_days: firm commitment to pay on time at 30 days net (fix our 97 % late-payment record)
trades.get: unit_price for part:350013 held at 1608.32 for 2027, no increase
trades.why: Costs us little beyond discipline and removes its main grievance and the threat to review conditions.

trades.give: volume_per_year: add part:350011 (IE3 7.5 kW, already qualified, quoted 421.06) plus a rolling forecast for part:350013
trades.get: unit_price reduction of up to 2 % on part:350013 (within the account manager's authority) and better pricing on part:350011
trades.why: It explicitly rewards customers with volume; bundling makes us bigger without needing committee approval.

trades.give: contract_months: renew the framework for 24–36 months
trades.get: lead_time_days 42 guaranteed as a delivery commitment (not 'from stock only') and price fixed per year
trades.why: Longer commitment counters the 'not strategic' view and secures our only active source.

arguments.point: We are a stable, growing account of about 1.15 M EUR a year with zero complaints and zero ppm. We want to consolidate more motor volume with them, not less.
Under the framework, price changes need written notice at least 90 days before year-end, i.e. by 2 Oct 2026. The latest quote confirms the unchanged 1608.32, so 2027 should stay at this price.
Past renewals settled close to zero (-1.5 %, 0.0 %, +1.7 %), so a price hold is the established norm.
Keep any requested price move at or below 2 % so their account manager can agree without committee approval.
We acknowledge the late payments and commit to correcting them. This should land with them as respect for their terms.

avoid: Threatening to switch or cut volume: we are 0.6 % of their turnover and they already call us 'not strategic'.
Asking for longer payment terms or skonto-style extras while we pay 19 days late on average.
Demanding cuts above 2 %, which trigger the pricing committee and delays.
Leaning hard on should-cost: their price is only +2.6 % above cost:350013, and that estimate has 5 % confidence.
Tight ultimatums: their replies are already slow, and pressure invites de-prioritisation.
tone: Businesslike and constructive. Present us as a reliable partner that wants to grow and is fixing its payment behaviour, with clear, simple, low-effort proposals.
red_flags: Walk-away risk: the framework auto-extends unless terminated by about 2 Oct 2026 (90 days before 31 Dec). Given the 'not strategic' remark, the supplier could terminate or de-prioritise us.
Service downgrade already visible: 'list conditions; supply from stock only' and slower replies since summer.
Our late payment (97 % late, mean 19.4 days) may trigger a review of their conditions.
Single active source for part:350013 (100 % quota); only one other source is listed. We should secure supply and prepare the alternative.
OTD dipped to 92.3 % in two quarters, below the 95 % target, although quality is otherwise excellent.

evidence.claim: Group-owned; account manager can move up to 2 %, the pricing committee handles anything above.
Refocusing on key accounts; our volume is called 'not strategic' and replies are slower.
Supplier complained about overdue invoices and threatened to review conditions.
Latest quote for part:350013 is unchanged at 1608.32, list conditions, supply from stock only.
Price is +2.6 % over the no-margin should-cost estimate (low confidence).
Excellent quality: 0 ppm and green scores in all four quarters.
Framework runs to 2026-12-31, auto-extends 12 months, 90-day notice; prices fixed per calendar year.
Part:350011 is already qualified at this supplier and quoted at 421.06, offering potential for volume bundling.

indicators.credit_index: 171 (12 months ago 171; higher is worse, >300 weak)
price_vs_should_cost_no_margin: part:350013: price 1608.32 vs cost:350013 1567.9 (its own plant): +2.6 %
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 92.3, ppm 0) → 2026Q1 green (otd 92.3, ppm 0) → 2026Q2 green (otd 100.0, ppm 0) → 2026Q3 green (otd 95.8, ppm 0)
